item.title: Pennsylvania woman dies of measles complications, coroner reports
item.description: A 40-year-old woman died on Saturday from complications associated with measles, the coroner reported.

item.title: Trump blames rise in diesel prices on Ukrainian strikes against Russian oil refineries
item.description: President Trump is demanding that Ukraine stop targeting Russian oil refineries, claiming the strikes are raising the price of diesel. CBS News' Ed O'Keefe and Aaron MacLean have more.

item.title: Iconic designer Bob Mackie dies at 87. See photos of legendary stars he dressed.
item.description: Dubbed the "Designer to the Stars," Bob Mackie won nine Emmy Awards, a Tony Award and was nominated for three Oscars.

item.title: Understanding the potential risks of untamed AI
item.description: Several leaders of the artificial intelligence industry are calling for government regulation and a slowdown in development. Machine Intelligence Research Institute President Nate Soares joins "The Takeout" with his reaction. Then, CBS News senior White House and political correspondent Ed O'Keefe joins with President Trump's perspective.

item.title: CBS News interviews so-called AI actor Tilly Norwood on upcoming movie "Misaligned"
item.description: The first so-called AI actor, Tilly Norwood, is on a promotional tour for an upcoming movie produced by a British company. CBS News correspondent Leigh Kiniry interviewed the AI on the film "Misaligned."

item.title: Trump administration expands its "third country" deportations
item.description: The Trump administration is expanding its "third country" deportations, or a process in which an undocumented immigrant is deported to a third country to which they have no connection. CBS News immigration correspondent Camilo Montoya-Galvez reports from Liberia, one of more than 30 nations receiving deportees from the U.S.

item.title: Trump dismisses push for AI guardrails despite warnings from tech leaders
item.description: President Trump threw cold water on momentum for AI guardrails, saying all the U.S. needs is a "SMART PRESIDENT."

item.title: Anthropic co-founder says the governments should play a role in AI regulation
item.description: Anthropic co-founder Jack Clark is the latest tech leader to speak out about regulating AI. He told the BBC in an exclusive interview that the private companies should work with governments on policy. Washington Post reporter Gerrit De Vynck joins CBS News to discuss.

item.title: Stocks start week in negative territory as Saudi oil pipeline goes down and AI warnings persist
item.description: Stocks started the week in negative territory as high gas prices and recent warnings from tech leaders about artificial intelligence spooked investors. Matt Phillips, markets correspondent for Axios, joins CBS News with analysis.

item.title: Tech stocks slump after AI execs call for industry slowdown
item.description: The Nasdaq slid 1% on Monday after AI company executives called for a slowdown in developing the technology.

item.title: Oil prices stay above $100 as Iran and Oman delay Strait of Hormuz talks
item.description: Iran and Oman delayed a meeting to discuss control of the Strait of Hormuz as fighting between Iran's Houthi allies and Saudi Arabia raises the stakes for global energy markets.

item.title: Ross Fire still burning, with over 90,000 acres scorched
item.description: The wildfire, which has torn through Palo Pinto and Jack counties, forced evacuations, closed roads and disrupted schools.

item.title: Here's how much interest a $150,000 2-year CD account can earn now
item.description: A 2-year CD account of this size could provide ample financial protection and a big return when it matures in 2028.

item.title: The AI bubble is leaking air, some economists say. Should investors worry?
item.description: AI has fueled a stock boom in recent years. Now, some Wall Street analysts think that epic run is coming to an end.

item.title: Abbott Labs to pay nearly $385M in case over bacterial contamination at plant
item.description: The case stems from a Cronobacter bacterial contamination at one of Abbott Laboratories' Michigan plants.

item.title: Understanding the concerns of the AI race with China
item.description: President Trump criticized Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei's AI warnings and said the U.S. must maintain its lead over China in the AI race. CBS News national security contributor Sam Vinograd joins to discuss.

item.title: EPA to eliminate limits on climate pollution from power plants
item.description: The rule, which is expected to face immediate legal challenges, also could prevent future administrations from regulating greenhouse gas emissions from power plants, sources said.

item.title: Brokers offer felons path to Trump pardons for high cost, CBS News investigation finds
item.description: Paid brokers are now offering felons a path to be pardoned by President Trump, a CBS News investigation shows. CBS News' Gabe Kaminsky and Daniel Klaidman have more on their 60 Minutes report.

item.title: Biosecurity expert on why Anthropic report on AI misuse is "pretty concerning"
item.description: Dr. Ashish Jha, founder of BioRadar and a senior fellow at Harvard's Belfer Center, joins to discuss Anthropic's recent report about how it blocked bad actors from using its Claude models to design biological weapons.

item.title: What are the monthly payments on a $250,000 home equity loan if opened this September?
item.description: Need to borrow $250,000 from your home equity? Here's how much a loan can cost if taken out in today's rate climate.

item.title: The U.S. economy faces mounting headwinds. Here are the top risks.
item.description: Rising energy costs, persistently high inflation and mounting federal debt are clouding the outlook for the U.S. economy — and Americans' finances.

item.title: Trump blames rising diesel price on Russia-Ukraine war
item.description: President Trump said on social media that the rising diesel price is mostly due to the Russia-Ukraine war and not Iran. CBS News' Aidan Stretch has more.

item.title: Trump dismisses AI leaders' warnings, slams Anthropic CEO in social media post
item.description: President Trump downplayed recent warnings from leaders of major AI firms about tech regulation and development. In a post on Truth Social, he accused Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei of "pretending to be a 'perfect little angel.'" CBS News' Caitlin Huey-Burns has more.

item.title: Vance says 870K people suspected of COVID-era U.S. fraud barred from federal loans
item.description: A U.S. enforcement push, dubbed "Heartland fraud surge," probed losses involving the Paycheck Protection Program and Economic Injury Disaster Loan program.

item.title: As AI rhetoric heats up, Congress stalls on action
item.description: Some House Democrats are calling on Speaker Mike Johnson to delay the congressional recess expected at the end of the week until lawmakers pass AI safeguards.

item.title: U.S. Air Force officer shot down in Iran says watching crewman's rescue was "proudest dad moment"
item.description: For the season premiere of "60 Minutes," Norah O'Donnell interviewed the U.S. Air Force officer who was stuck in Iran for more than two days after his F-15 was downed. From his vantage point, he witnessed the rescue of his crewmate.

item.title: Air Force officer shot down in Iran says he was grateful watching crewmate get rescued
item.description: The Air Force colonel who spent two days evading capture after Iran shot down his F-15E sat down with Norah O'Donnell in a 60 Minutes interview. He recalled the moment he saw his fellow crewmate being saved as he hid. CBS News national security analyst Aaron Maclean joins to share what stood out to him in the interview.

item.title: Even with Rams a Super Bowl favorite, coach Sean McVay is "tormented"
item.description: With the Rams a Super Bowl favorite as the season kicks off, coach Sean McVay is forging ahead, having learned from past successes and failures.

item.title: Pardon brokers offer to "put pressure on the president," at sky-high costs
item.description: Hidden cameras captured lobbyists as they tried to woo a potential client interested in obtaining a pardon from President Trump.

item.title: Trump admin. to send $500 checks to nearly 1 million ACA enrollees
item.description: Affordable Care Act recipients in 30 states are set to receive the $500 checks starting in October. Here's why.
